label: Terrain dock minimized
verdict:
**Not clean — 4 issues found.**

### Overlap / clipping
1. **Sidebar collides with status bar (bottom-left).** The "Patios & Paths" section's first item ("Patio", ~y766) sits inside the full-width status bar zone ("Tool: Raise | Brush: 8 ft…" at ~y760). The status bar spans from x=0, so the sidebar's last visible list item is clipped/overlapping the status-bar text. The sidebar's scroll area should end above the status bar.

2. **Bottom-center control stack is cramped.** The "Terrain Sculpting" window (closes ~y678), the Sculpt ▶/command row (~y690–724), and the scale bar + Sun button (~y727–757) stack directly on each other; the Sun button appears to just touch the status-bar edge. Not literally overlapping, but zero breathing room and visually jumbled.

### 5-second comprehension
3. **Heavy duplicate controls.** Left floating rail has Terrain / Analyze / Measure / Sun & Shadow; the bottom row repeats Terrain / Analyze / Tape Measure / Sun. A new user can't tell which set is authoritative or active (status bar says "Tool: Raise," but no visible control is labeled "Raise" — presumably buried in the Sculpt ▶ dropdown). Also, the header defaults to **Advanced**, the Getting Started tip only explains the drag-and-drop catalog, and nothing explains the sculpting toolset — two competing mental models (catalog app vs. terrain editor) with no onboarding for the latter.

### Confusing / suspicious labels
4. **"Innovate" (bottom-right button)** — almost certainly a typo for "Irrigate" in a backyard-yard context; as written it's meaningless here. (If it's intentional AI-suggest, the bulb icon doesn't resolve the ambiguity.)

### Notably broken-looking
5. **"FPS: 1"** in the status bar. Even if it's a live readout, displaying 1 FPS makes the app look stalled/broken; worth verifying the renderer isn't actually stuck, and masking the readout when it hasn't updated.

### Minor polish
- Redo is correctly disabled; header, sidebar catalog, compass, "Daytime" pill, and right-edge zoom buttons look fine.
- "Underground" is cryptic as a top-level sculpt mode — consider "Utilities" or a tooltip.

**Fix priority:** #1 (actual overlap) → #5 (looks broken) → #4 (label) → #3/#2 (comprehension/spacing).
